diagnosis.summary: Payment-service is severely degraded, with p95 latency rising from 110 ms to 2900 ms (26.4x). Order-service is reflecting this degradation, with its own p95 latency at 2950 ms against a 130 ms baseline and a 5xx error rate of 16.7%. The incident has been active for 2 minutes.
diagnosis.root_cause: A severe slowdown within payment-service is the most likely root cause. Order-service calls payment-service on every POST /orders, so payment-service latency spiking 26.4x above baseline propagated directly into order-service dependency latency and then into order-service 5xx errors, which appeared 40 seconds after payment-service latency rose (observed sequence from correlated timestamps).
evidence: Payment-service p95 latency rose from 110 ms to 2900 ms, a 26.4x increase.
Order-service p95 dependency latency (time spent calling payment-service) rose from 112 ms to 2950 ms, a 26.3x increase.
Order-service dependency error count rose from 0 to 57 per minute.
Order-service 5xx error rate rose from 0.0 to 16.7%.
Order-service p95 end-to-end latency rose from 130 ms to 2950 ms, a 22.7x increase.
Payment-service p95 latency rose above its baseline at 14:32:00; order-service 5xx errors rose above their baseline at 14:32:40, 40 seconds later (observed sequence).
recommended_actions: Inspect payment-service Lambda logs and error traces starting at 14:32:00 to identify what is causing the latency spike.
Check payment-service Lambda concurrency and throttle metrics to determine whether the function is being starved of capacity.
Consider adding or lowering a timeout on order-service calls to payment-service so that slow payment calls fail fast and reduce cascading latency into order-service.
If payment-service cannot be recovered quickly, evaluate temporarily returning a degraded response from order-service (e.g. queuing orders) to stop the 16.7% 5xx rate from reaching customers.
Review payment-service recent deployments or configuration changes that coincide with the 14:32:00 start time.
